dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2501.text: To stretch out. Formed from 舍 and 予, with 予 also indicating the sound. Another explanation: 舒 means slow or relaxed.

shuowen:2502.text: To deceive and bewilder one another. From reversed 予. The Book of Zhou says: “Let none fabricate deceptions to create illusions.”

shuowen:2503.text: To drive away. Formed from 攴, with 方 indicating the sound. All graphs in the 放 group contain 放.

shuowen:2504.text: To go out roaming. From 出 and 放.

shuowen:2505.text: Light and shadows flowing. From 白 and 放. Read like 龠.

shuowen:2506.text: Things falling; passing something between above and below. From 爪 and 又. All graphs in the 𠬪 group contain 𠬪. Read like 摽 in the Odes' “Plums are falling.”

shuowen:2507.text: To draw or pull. From 𠬪 and 于. Large-seal writing uses it for the carriage-shaft character 轅.

shuowen:2508.text: To put in order: little children in disorder, with 𠬪 ordering them. Pronounced the same as 亂. Another explanation: to arrange.

shuowen:2509.text: To hand to one another. Formed from 𠬪, with abbreviated 舟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2510.text: To gather in a pinch. From 𠬪 and 己.

shuowen:2511.text: To pull. From 𠬪 and 𠂆.

shuowen:2512.text: That on which one relies. From 𠬪 and 工. Pronounced the same as 隱.

shuowen:2513.text: To hold with five fingers. Formed from 𠬪, with 一 indicating the sound. Read like 律.

shuowen:2514.text: To advance and take. Formed from 𠬪, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2515.text: To damage and pierce. From 又 and 歺. All graphs in the 𣦼 group contain 𣦼. Read like 殘.

shuowen:2516.text: A ditch. From 𣦼 and 谷. Read like 郝.

shuowen:2517.text: The intention of probing something hard. From 𣦼 and 貝; 貝 is a hard treasure. Read like 概. [The opening phrase 𣦼探堅 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2518.text: A pit. Formed from 𣦼 and 井, with 井 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:2519.text: Deep understanding; penetration. From 𣦼, 目 and abbreviated 谷.

shuowen:2520.text: The remains of split bones. From half of 冎. All graphs in the 歺 group contain 歺. Read like 櫱 in 櫱岸.

shuowen:2521.text: Illness. Formed from 歺, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2522.text: Dazed or confused. Formed from 歺, with 昬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2523.text: A fetus failing or perishing. Formed from 歺, with 𧶠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2524.text: To end. Formed from 歺, with 勿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2525.text: The death of a grandee is called 𣨛. Formed from 歺, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2526.text: To die or be put to death. Formed from 歺, with 朱 indicating the sound. Han ordinances say: “When a chief of the Man or Yi has committed a crime, he should be put to death.”

shuowen:2527.text: A fetus failing or perishing. Formed from 歺, with 𥁕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2528.text: Not reaching adulthood. Death at nineteen through sixteen is “upper 殤”; fifteen through twelve, “middle 殤”; eleven through eight, “lower 殤.” Formed from 歺, with abbreviated 傷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2529.text: To depart, to die. Formed from 歺, with 且 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Xun then died.”

shuowen:2530.text: To put to death. Formed from 歺, with 亟 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “He executed Gun at Mount Yu.”

shuowen:2531.text: To die. Formed from 歺, with 壹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2532.text: The desolation and silence of death. Formed from 歺, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2533.text: The dead in a coffin awaiting removal for burial, treated as a guest. Formed from 歺 and 賓, with 賓 also indicating the sound. The Xia placed the coffin at the eastern steps, the Yin between the two pillars, and the Zhou at the guest steps.

shuowen:2534.text: To bury. Formed from 歺, with 隶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2535.text: A dead person on the road whom someone covers. Formed from 歺, with 堇 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “When a dead person lies on the road, someone may yet cover them.”

shuowen:2536.text: The smell of decay. Formed from 歺, with 臭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2537.text: To rot. Formed from 歺, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2538.text: To decay. Formed from 歺, with 丂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2539.text: Danger. Formed from 歺, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2540.text: Calamity or blame. Formed from 歺, with 央 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2541.text: To harm. Formed from 歺, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2542.text: To exhaust or destroy completely. Formed from 歺, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2543.text: To destroy even the smallest remainder. Formed from 歺, with 韱 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The Qi men were annihilated at Sui.”

shuowen:2544.text: To exhaust completely. Formed from 歺, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2545.text: To ruin. Formed from 歺, with 睪 indicating the sound. The Book of Shang says: “The constant human relations were ruined.”

shuowen:2546.text: An epidemic illness of livestock. From 歺 and 羸.

shuowen:2547.text: To kill a sheep and remove its fetus. Formed from 歺, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2548.text: Remains left after birds and beasts have eaten. From 歺 and 肉.

shuowen:2549.text: Fat and grease left a long time, apparently decaying. Formed from 歺, with 直 indicating the sound. [The precise sense of 久殖 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2550.text: Withered. Formed from 歺, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2551.text: To abandon. Formed from 歺, with 奇 indicating the sound. Common speech calls death 大㱦.

shuowen:2552.text: To be extinguished: that from which a person departs. From 歺 and 人. All graphs in the 死 group contain 死.

shuowen:2553.text: The death of a duke or marquis. Formed from 死, with abbreviated 瞢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2554.text: The dwelling place of the dead. Formed from 死, with abbreviated 蒿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2555.text: Seeing blood in battle is called injury; derangement may be called unconsciousness; dying and returning to life is 𣣌. Formed from 死, with 次 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2556.text: To strip off a person's flesh and leave the bones. A pictograph, with the projecting head-bone. All graphs in the 冎 group contain 冎.

shuowen:2557.text: To divide and dismember. From 冎 and 刀.

shuowen:2558.text: To separate. Formed from 冎, with 卑 indicating the sound. Read like 罷.

shuowen:2559.text: The core of flesh. From 冎 with 肉. All graphs in the 骨 group contain 骨.

shuowen:2560.text: 髑髏: the skull. Formed from 骨, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2561.text: The skull, 髑髏. Formed from 骨, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2562.text: The shoulder blade. Formed from 骨, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2563.text: The front of the shoulder. Formed from 骨, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2564.text: Joined ribs. Formed from 骨, with 并 indicating the sound. Duke Wen of Jin had joined ribs.

shuowen:2565.text: The thigh. Formed from 骨, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2566.text: The thighbone. Formed from 骨, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2567.text: The buttock bone. Formed from 骨, with 厥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2568.text: The region above the thigh. Formed from 骨, with 寬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2569.text: The tip of the knee. Formed from 骨, with 賓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2570.text: The end of a bone. Formed from 骨, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2571.text: The bone between knee and shank. Formed from 骨, with 䝿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2572.text: The shank. Formed from 骨, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2573.text: The shank, 骹. Formed from 骨, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2574.text: The shinbone. Formed from 骨, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2575.text: Fat within bone. Formed from 骨, with 隓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2576.text: Yellow fluid between bones. Formed from 骨, with 易 indicating the sound. Read like 惕 in the Changes' “At evening, vigilant as if in danger.”

shuowen:2577.text: The totality of the twelve bodily divisions. Formed from 骨, with 豊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2578.text: Paralysis affecting one side. Formed from 骨, with 麻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2579.text: A food bone lodged in the throat. Formed from 骨, with 㪅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2580.text: The bones of birds and beasts are called 骼. Formed from 骨, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2581.text: The remaining bones of birds and beasts are called 骴; 骴 suggests repulsiveness. Formed from 骨, with 此 indicating the sound. The Bright Hall Monthly Ordinances says: “Cover exposed bones and bury remains.” 骴 is alternatively formed from 肉.

shuowen:2582.text: A curved or crooked bone-end, 骫奊. Formed from 骨, with 丸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2583.text: A bone pin that gathers the hair. Formed from 骨, with 會 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The jeweled cap pins are like stars.”

shuowen:2584.text: Cut flesh. A pictograph. All graphs in the 肉 group contain 肉.

shuowen:2585.text: The first signs of a woman's pregnancy. Formed from 肉, with 某 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2586.text: A woman's pregnancy at one month. Formed from 肉, with 不 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2587.text: A woman's pregnancy at three months. Formed from 肉, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2588.text: Flesh. Formed from 肉, with 几 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2589.text: Skin. Formed from 肉, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2590.text: The cheek region of the face. Formed from 肉, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2591.text: Cheek flesh. Formed from 肉, with 幾 indicating the sound. Read like 畿.

shuowen:2592.text: The edge of the mouth. Formed from 肉, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2593.text: The neck. Formed from 肉, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2594.text: Above the heart and below the diaphragm. Formed from 肉, with 亡 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “The disease is below the 肓.”

shuowen:2595.text: The organ of water. Formed from 肉, with 臤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2596.text: The organ of metal. Formed from 肉, with 巿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2597.text: The organ of earth. Formed from 肉, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2598.text: The organ of wood. Formed from 肉, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2599.text: The repository connected to the liver. Formed from 肉, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:2600.text: The repository of grain. From 肉; 𡇒 is pictographic.
